decisions.reason: Holding the defensive risk-premia book (BRK-B 16, UNH 12, USMV 10, SVXY 4, 58% cash) unchanged. Research done via web search: the week's damage is an AI/semiconductor-led liquidation plus Fed minutes floating a larger-than-usual December hike; I could not find a wrap of the 11-20 session itself, so the latest marks come from my packet. The book is +1.6% lifetime against SPY at about -7%, and it is already only 42% gross, so the structure did its job and I see no reason to pay to change it at what may be a capitulation low. Leg by leg: (1) UNH -17.5% is the real wound. The cause is the CMS CRUSH proposed Medicare Advantage audit rule of 11-16 - a proposal, not a final rule, with comments open to 2027-01-19; a Texas federal court vacated the comparable framework in September 2025, Oppenheimer expects litigation again, the projected recoveries are concentrated in 2028-2030, and insurers can reprice bids if it survives. That is a headline shock to a value leg, not a broken thesis, and selling a quality-value name after a 20% policy-driven drop is harvesting the premium backwards. I am not adding either: no company response yet and the stock fell a further 3% after the 11-18 close, so 12% stays 12% with the -30% stop from the original fill as the hard exit. (2) SVXY -14.4% with VIX in the mid-20s: the volatility risk premium is richest right after a spike, the sleeve is only 4%, and its -20% stop is about 6.5% away - if the selloff extends it closes itself for under 0.3% of NAV more. (3) BRK-B and USMV fell about half as much as the index, which is exactly what the quality and min-vol sleeves are for; their stops are intact. Still no TLT: the Fed is hiking, so the term-premium sleeve stays out. Novelty rule: no shared symbols with my Round 2 book (XLP, WMT, XLV, LLY), so same-direction overlap is 0%.

A mandate-consistent, diversified small-cap growth starter at 20% captures part of any oversold rebound after seven down sessions while capping the book-level risk of a further leg down at roughly 2% of NAV via a 10% stop.
